title: One Joint Too Many: The Null Space of a Seven Joint Arm, Moving the Elbow While the Hand Stays, and Steering Away From the Limits

questions.question: What is the null space of a seven joint arm's Jacobian?
options: Joint motions that the tool does not feel
The joint motions that move the tool most
The set of poses with one solution
questions.explanation: Seven joint rates map to six tool velocities, so one combination of joint rates maps to nothing. The elbow can swing while the hand stays.

questions.question: A joint motion put through the null space was felt by the tool at:
questions.explanation: For the seven joint Panda the projected motion left the tool still to ten decimal places. For the six joint UR5 almost nothing is left over to project.

questions.question: Starting 0.086 of its range from its limit, the margin became:
options: 0.156 while the tool stayed within 0.00037 m
questions.explanation: The joints moved 0.66 rad toward the middle of their ranges through the null space, and the tool stayed within 0.37 mm.

questions.question: Without a correction on the tool, it drifted:
options: Not at all: the null space is exact
questions.explanation: The null space is that of the Jacobian at one pose. Over finite steps the arm's curvature shows, and the tool creeps unless its error is corrected each step.

questions.question: Why must a preferred joint motion be projected?
options: Added directly, it moves the tool: 1.244 m/s against 0.00000000
Unprojected, it has no effect on the joints
Projection keeps the joints inside their limits
questions.explanation: Any joint motion moves the tool unless the part the tool feels is taken out. Added raw it moved the tool at 1.244 m/s; projected, not at all.

questions.question: What is wrong with an unclamped solution that reaches the pose?
options: It took more steps than the clamped one
It may need a joint outside its limit, which the arm cannot do: 0.283 rad outside
questions.explanation: It reached the pose with joint 6 0.283 rad past its limit. An answer the arm cannot take is wrong however small its error.
